Clinical Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with
complaints of neck pain and restricted cervical range of motion. The reported injury
is consistent in type and mechanism with the force of this impact. Over the course of
eleven visits, care proceeded along a typical conservative pathway, including manual
therapy, stretching, and a home exercise program. Symptoms improved steadily, and
visit frequency was tapered as function returned.
On examination, paraspinal muscle tenderness and reduced cervical rotation were noted,
supporting the presence of a soft tissue injury. Other components of the neurological
and orthopedic assessment were within normal limits, with no motor deficit, no sensory
change, and negative provocative testing. No prior injury or treatment involving the
cervical region is known to this provider. Billing records reflect single charges for
each service rendered, with no duplicated or repeated entries.
Current assessment is cervical strain, improving. Discharge from active care is
anticipated pending completion of the home program, with follow-up as needed for any
recurrence of symptoms.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
